games.title: Pay Your Deeds
games.short:
Pay Your Deeds is a roguelike deck-builder played on a 5×4 slot reel.

You are in debt, and every few days the Sector expects another payment.

Spin the reel, collect Scrap Credits and add new Symbols to your build. Find combinations that work together, remove the ones that don't, and try to make enough money before your next Deed is due.

If you can't pay, the run is over.
description: Build the reel. Pay the debt. Survive another day.
Every purchase will receive a Steam key when the Steam version becomes available.
Pay Your Deeds is a roguelike deck-builder played on a 5×4 slot reel.
You are in debt, and every few days the Sector expects another payment.
Spin the reel, collect Scrap Credits and add new Symbols to your build. Find combinations that work together, remove the ones that don't, and try to make enough money before your next Deed is due.
If you can't pay, the run is over.
BUILD YOUR REEL
Your reel starts simple.
During a run you'll add Symbols, remove bad ones and slowly turn your build into something that can keep up with the increasing payments.
Symbols can generate resources, multiply values, consume other Symbols, destroy them, transform them or trigger effects from other parts of your reel.
A good build isn't about collecting every strong Symbol you find. Sometimes adding one more thing is exactly what ruins it.
WHAT'S IN THE GAME
100+ Symbols with different effects, rarities and interactions.
24 Deeds with increasingly difficult payment requirements.
5 creditor factions with their own identity and progression.
35 Power Store upgrades.
20 Side Contracts.
Multiple Clearance Levels and progression systems.
Reroll, remove and modify your Symbol pool during a run.
Endless Mode for builds that survive past the normal game.
Persistent local statistics, records and achievements.
Fully playable offline.
EVERY RUN GOES SOMEWHERE DIFFERENT
You might start with a few Medical Symbols and end up building around Rot.
You might turn Tools into a Tech engine, use Hazards as fuel, or build something around Animals, Trade, Power, Arsenal or Salvage.
The archetypes aren't classes. They are pieces you can mix together depending on what the run gives you.
The strongest Symbol isn't always the one your build needs.
THE SECTOR
The entire game takes place inside Sector XP, a decaying early-2000s operating system.
Your Deeds, mail, contracts, upgrades, faction messages and run records all exist inside the same machine.
It isn't just a menu between runs. It's where the game lives.

updates.title: Pay your Deeds - 1.1.0 - DEMO RELEASE
updates.text:
A new Demo version of Pay Your Deeds is now available.

With the game continuing to grow, I wanted there to be a proper way for new players to experience the core gameplay before purchasing the full version.

The Demo is not a separate experimental build or an outdated version of the game. It is based on the current game and has been specifically configured to provide a limited but representative introduction to the full experience.

What is available in the Demo?

The Demo includes access to:

  • Campaign Mode
  • Clearance 01
  • The core gameplay loop
  • Available Symbols and progression mechanics within the Demo
  • Upgrades and systems encountered during Clearance 01
  • The main gameplay structure of Pay Your Deeds

The game may still display some of the content available beyond the Demo so players can see what exists in the full version.

However:

  • Clearance 02–10 are not available in the Demo
  • Endless Mode is not available in the Demo
  • UNKNOWN Mode is not available in the Demo

Attempting to access restricted content will clearly indicate that it is not available in the Demo.

The Demo also uses its own progression data, allowing it to exist independently from the full game without interfering with full-version saves.

Full Game Price Update

Alongside the release of the Demo, the price of Pay Your Deeds has been updated to:

$9.99 USD

The game has changed considerably throughout development, with more content, systems, balancing work, platform support and improvements being added over time.

The new price is intended to better represent the current state and scope of the full game while still keeping it accessible.

Steam Release Coming Soon

I am also preparing Pay Your Deeds for release on Steam.

The Steam page is currently being worked on and it will have Windows and Linux support planned for the release on Steam.

More information about the Steam launch, availability and release details will be posted as everything gets closer to being ready.

Development will continue with bug fixes, balancing improvements, polish and additional work where needed.

Thank you to everyone who has supported the project, purchased the game, tested builds, reported issues or suggested improvements.

If you haven't played Pay Your Deeds yet, the Demo is now the easiest way to give it a try and see whether the full game is for you.

games.title: Sector Rot
games.short:
The Sector is alive. Every expedition can be your last.

Sector Rot is a tactical ASCII survival game about exploring a hostile, persistent world filled with mutants, armed factions, toxic ruins, abandoned structures and catastrophic Emissions.
description: The Sector is alive. Every expedition can be your last.
Sector Rot is a tactical ASCII survival game about exploring a hostile, persistent world filled with mutants, armed factions, toxic ruins, abandoned structures and catastrophic Emissions.
Leave the safety of your shelter, scavenge for weapons and supplies, accept dangerous contracts, explore unknown sectors and decide how far you are willing to push before turning back.

Combat is dangerous and information matters. Your field of view is limited, enemies can hear and pursue you, ammunition is valuable, wounds can quickly change a fight and sometimes surviving means avoiding a battle entirely.
Open Run
Open Run is the main sandbox survival experience of Sector Rot.

Create a world from a seed, choose its size and begin with limited resources in a living network of connected sectors. Roads, structures, safe locations, faction territory, enemies, loot, hazards and other world elements are generated from that seed.
The same seed and world settings generate the same world, allowing you to replay, share or explore specific worlds again.
Open Run worlds can include:
Multiple connected sectors with different layouts and conditions
Road networks, ruins, shelters, compounds and points of interest
Mutant populations with different behaviours and senses
Human factions, patrols, guarded territory and conflicts
Contracts, traders, reputation and progression
Dynamic world conditions and dangerous Emissions
Long-term objectives that extend far beyond simple survival
Your actions can affect your relationship with the factions around you. Survive long enough, build your reputation, secure territory and work toward establishing your own place inside the Sector.
Tactical Survival
Sector Rot combines deliberate grid-based movement with a world that continues to operate around you.
Tactical movement and positioning
Real-time world clock and environmental systems
Limited field of view and perception
Different mutant senses, behaviours and attack patterns
Weapons with their own ammunition and combat characteristics
Armor, medical supplies, loot and inventory management
Toxic environments and dangerous areas
Emissions that force you to find proper shelter
Safehouses and structures that can become essential during expeditions
Running directly toward every enemy is rarely the best solution. Positioning, preparation and knowing when to retreat are just as important as your weapon.
Campaign
Alongside Open Run, Sector Rot includes a more structured Campaign experience with authored progression and objectives.
Choose a character class, learn the rules of the Sector and take on increasingly dangerous expeditions as more of the world and its systems are revealed.
Characters & Progression
Multiple starting classes with different strengths
Perks and character progression
Persistent player statistics
Achievements
Faction reputation
Contracts and expedition objectives
Weapons, ammunition, equipment and scavenged resources
Multiplayer
Sector Rot also supports cooperative multiplayer built around the same world and survival systems used by Open Run.
LAN multiplayer
Direct IP multiplayer
Co-op Open Run worlds
Shared world state and survival systems
Multiplayer world progression
The goal is for single-player and multiplayer to follow the same fundamental rules instead of treating multiplayer as a separate simplified game mode.
Pure ASCII Presentation
The entire game is designed around an ASCII / terminal-inspired visual identity.
ASCII environments and structures
ASCII characters, mutants and effects
Terminal-style menus and interface
Readable tactical information without replacing the ASCII identity
Configurable display, controls and accessibility options
Under the simple visual language is a simulation built around exploration, survival, AI behaviour, factions, procedural worlds and persistent systems.
Modding & Map Making
Sector Rot includes optional creator tools for players who want to build their own content.
Public Map Maker for creating and validating custom ASCII maps
Modding Kit for creating custom gameplay content
Custom classes, weapons, enemies and loot
Custom campaigns and game modes
Custom icons, colours and audio
The creator tools are completely optional. You only need the main game to play Sector Rot.
Alpha Development
Sector Rot is currently in active Alpha development.
Systems are still being expanded, balanced and improved. Bugs can happen, features may change and some parts of the game are still being developed.
Current development is focused on improving Open Run, world generation, performance, multiplayer, AI, content variety, quality-of-life features and the overall stability of the game.
If something breaks, feels unfair or simply does not make sense, please report it. Player feedback is extremely valuable during development.

updates.title: Sector Rot - Alpha 0.9.0 - Factions & Deeds
updates.text:
Open Run, Freehold, Living World & Multiplayer Overhaul

Hello everyone!

Alpha 0.9.0 is one of the biggest updates Sector Rot has received so far.

Since Alpha 0.8.0, a huge amount of work has gone into rebuilding the foundations of Open Run, world generation, factions, progression, multiplayer, the PDA, accessibility, UI stability and the general survival experience.

This update is not just about adding more content.

It is about making Sector Rot feel more like an actual living world where your actions matter, factions remember you, sectors evolve, and an Open Run can eventually become your own story.

OPEN RUN — MAJOR REWORK

Open Run has received a large overhaul.

The world now continues to live around the player while movement keeps the tactical turn-based feeling of Sector Rot.

Player movement remains controlled by turns, while other world systems can continue in real time.

Holding a movement key also correctly continues movement turn by turn instead of requiring repeated individual presses.

Open Run now includes:

  • Improved sector population
  • More points of interest
  • More environmental landmarks
  • Better hostile population distribution
  • Improved roads and sector connections
  • More camps and compounds
  • More loot opportunities
  • More faction presence
  • Improved safe zones
  • Better world persistence
  • More meaningful exploration

Easy difficulty has also been rebalanced so sectors no longer feel unnecessarily empty while still remaining more forgiving than the higher difficulties.

NEW PROCEDURAL WORLD GENERATION

Sector generation has received one of its largest upgrades yet.

Structures are no longer simply placed randomly into empty spaces.

The generator now creates locations using actual layout rules.

The generation process considers things such as:

  • Sector type
  • Roads
  • District purpose
  • Building roles
  • Entrances
  • Courtyards
  • Defensive positions
  • Cover
  • Loot
  • NPC population
  • Nearby points of interest

Different types of locations can now generate completely different layouts.

Examples include:

  • Residential streets
  • Residential courtyards
  • Industrial blocks
  • Workshop yards
  • Warehouse yards
  • Depots
  • Farmsteads
  • Research campuses
  • Clinics
  • Utility sites
  • Checkpoints
  • Scrap markets
  • Small survivor settlements

A warehouse area should now feel like a warehouse area.

A farm should contain structures appropriate for a farm.

Research locations can contain laboratories, offices and support buildings.

Industrial areas can include workshops, warehouses and utility structures.

Entrances are also placed with roads and courtyards in mind instead of simply being cut into a random wall.

FACTION LOCATIONS

Faction bases have also received improved generation rules.

Different factions can now favor different types of compounds and infrastructure instead of every faction receiving essentially the same base with a different name.

Faction-controlled locations may include combinations of:

  • Barracks
  • Workshops
  • Warehouses
  • Trade areas
  • Relay structures
  • Defensive courtyards
  • Research facilities
  • Utility buildings

Important faction locations are also guaranteed to contain meaningful infrastructure instead of occasionally generating as a single tiny building.

WORLD SIZES

Open Run supports multiple world sizes and long-term progression now scales with the selected world.

The larger the world, the larger the player's long-term objective becomes.

Current progression targets include:

Small World

24 Sector Deeds

Medium World

48 Sector Deeds

Large World

96 Sector Deeds

Massive World

160 Sector Deeds

Simply purchasing sectors in one straight line is not enough.

The player must establish control across multiple strategic regions of the world.

Larger worlds therefore require a larger and more distributed domain.

WORLD CONDITIONS

World Conditions have been repaired and expanded.

Individual conditions can now be enabled and disabled correctly.

The previous issue where one click could trigger the same option twice and immediately return it to its original state has been fixed.

The menu now supports:

  • Individual ON / OFF conditions
  • CUSTOM configurations
  • ALL
  • NONE

Changes are saved correctly and Multiplayer hosts can configure the same conditions without losing the rest of the server setup.

World Conditions can influence things such as:

  • Mutant activity
  • Bandit activity
  • Resource availability
  • Environmental danger
  • Visibility
  • Salvage opportunities
  • Anomalous activity

FACTIONS & REPUTATION

Faction progression has been expanded significantly.

The player can build relationships with the major organized factions through contracts, exploration and faction activity.

Reputation now matters much more because it is directly connected to long-term Open Run progression.

Hostile actions also have consequences.

Attacking faction members can reduce your reputation and change how that faction reacts to you.

Faction reputation is capped at:

100 / 100

CHARTERS

Before a faction allows you to legally purchase territory, you must first earn their trust.

To obtain a faction Charter you need:

  • At least 60 / 100 Reputation
  • At least 2 completed and claimed faction contracts

The Charter represents your permission to begin purchasing registered territory through that faction.

But a Charter alone is not enough to purchase a Deed.

SECTOR DEEDS

Sector Deeds are now one of the main long-term progression systems in Open Run.

A Deed represents ownership of a sector.

Purchasing territory is intentionally difficult.

To purchase a new Sector Deed you need:

  • 100 / 100 Reputation with the issuing faction
  • At least 4 completed and claimed contracts for that faction
  • The faction Charter
  • The sector must already have been visited
  • Access to the appropriate trader or quartermaster
  • A large amount of Scrap Credits

Deeds are designed to be expensive long-term investments.

Their price can increase depending on:

  • Sector value
  • Distance
  • Important locations
  • Trade activity
  • Frontier status
  • The amount of territory you already control

The more powerful your domain becomes, the more expensive expansion can become.

REGISTRY SERVICE CONTRACTS

Players now have a reliable way of reaching maximum faction reputation.

After completing enough work for a faction, additional Registry Service contracts can become available.

Examples include:

  • Field Security
  • Recovery Audits
  • Boundary Surveys

These contracts allow players to continue working toward 100 / 100 Reputation instead of being forced to wait for random world events.

YOUR OWN DOMAIN

Open Run now supports the concept of a personal domain.

Depending on your path through the world, your territory can represent either an independent organization or a branch connected to one of the existing factions.

Independent players can establish the:

Runner Freehold

Faction-aligned players can create their own territory while still maintaining their relationship with their chosen faction.

Territory ownership is persistent.

On the world map:

[P] represents territory controlled by you.

In Multiplayer:

[D] can represent territory controlled by another player's domain.

Black Road does not provide normal legal land registration like the organized factions.

PDA — FREEHOLD

The Freehold section of the PDA has been completely reorganized.

Instead of showing the player a wall of system information, the PDA now focuses on the things that actually matter while playing.

It can show:

  • Your current domain
  • Scrap Credits
  • Reputation
  • Charters
  • Completed contracts
  • Owned Deeds
  • Strategic regions
  • Long-term objective progress
  • What you still need for the next Deed
  • Recently acquired territory

The goal is simple:

The PDA should tell you:

What you have.

What you need.

What you should do next.

PLAYER GUIDE — OPEN RUN DEEDS

A new Player Guide topic has been added:

OPEN RUN DEEDS

It explains:

  • What a Charter is
  • What a Deed is
  • Reputation requirements
  • Contract requirements
  • How to purchase sectors
  • Why Deeds are expensive
  • Registry Service contracts
  • Territory markers
  • Multiplayer domains
  • Long-term Open Run progression

The Player Guide now contains 21 topics covering the major game systems.

THE LIVING ROT — OPEN RUN ENDGAME

Open Run now has an actual long-term conclusion.

After establishing enough influence, maintaining the necessary faction relationships and building a sufficiently large domain, the player can eventually reach the final Open Run objective.

A message appears in the PDA.

THE LIVING ROT

You have survived the sectors.

You have crossed faction borders.

You have fought the Rot.

You have built something inside it.

And eventually:

YOU ARE THE LIVING ROT.

At this point the player receives a final choice.

CONTINUE

Remain in the world as the Living Rot.

Keep your territory.

Continue exploring.

Continue expanding.

The Open Run remains active indefinitely.

SACRIFICE EVERYTHING

Give up everything you built.

Sacrifice your domain.

Destroy the Rot and begin restoring the sectors.

This becomes the true ending of that Open Run.

MULTIPLAYER OPEN RUN

The same Open Run foundations are being carried into Multiplayer.

Each player can have their own:

  • Reputation
  • Scrap Credits
  • Contracts
  • Charters
  • Sector Deeds
  • Territory
  • Faction alignment
  • Living Rot progression

One player does not have to own the entire server.

Multiple players can build their own domains inside the same world.

They can remain independent or align themselves with existing factions.

MULTIPLAYER ENDGAME

Completing your own Living Rot objective does not automatically shut down the server.

The player still receives their PDA message and personal progression milestone.

A global ending is controlled separately.

Only the host can initiate the final world sacrifice.

When this happens, connected players can vote.

If the vote fails:

The world continues.

If the vote succeeds:

The Rot is destroyed and the Multiplayer world reaches its conclusion.

MULTIPLAYER WORLD SYNCHRONIZATION

A large amount of work has also gone into keeping Open Run systems consistent between host and clients.

This includes improvements to:

  • World state
  • Emissions
  • Shelters
  • Sector state
  • Player domains
  • Territory ownership
  • Faction progression
  • Final vote state
  • Player progression

Emission schedules are now kept consistent between host and connected players.

PDA IMPROVEMENTS

The PDA has received many fixes and improvements.

This includes:

  • Improved Freehold page
  • Improved Territories page
  • Better faction information
  • Cleaner player-focused descriptions
  • Improved Expeditions
  • Better Large Text support
  • Stable PDA window sizing
  • Cleaner navigation

A major issue where opening:

PDA → EXPEDITIONS

could resize the game window has been fixed.

EXPEDITIONS

Expedition presentation has also been improved.

On Large Text mode the three expedition actions no longer attempt to squeeze long quest names into oversized buttons.

They now use compact actions such as:

[1] ACCEPT

[2] ACCEPT

[3] ACCEPT

The complete expedition name, danger, reward and description remain visible above them.

PLAYER-FACING INFORMATION CLEANUP

A large UI text pass has been completed.

Information that is useful to players remains visible.

This includes normal gaming terminology such as:

  • FPS
  • Ping / Latency
  • FOV
  • VFX
  • VSync
  • Resolution
  • Fullscreen
  • World Seed
  • Simulation
  • Damage values
  • Armor values
  • Loot bonuses
  • Healing bonuses
  • Prices

Internal development information is no longer unnecessarily shown to normal players.

HUD & HELP

The useful top-bar Help reminder has returned.

You can once again see:

[ H ] HELP

during gameplay.

The HUD can also display useful information such as:

  • FPS
  • Multiplayer Ping
  • Time
  • Co-op status

without filling the interface with internal diagnostic information.

LARGE TEXT & ACCESSIBILITY

Large Text support has received another major pass.

Dozens of screens have been checked for:

  • Clipped text
  • Oversized buttons
  • Broken navigation
  • Incorrect window resizing
  • Hidden options
  • Layout problems

Important screens such as:

  • PDA
  • Expeditions
  • Freehold
  • Player Guide
  • Settings
  • Multiplayer
  • Open Run Setup

have all received accessibility work.

SETTINGS

Settings and presentation options have been cleaned up and repaired.

Player-visible options continue to use familiar gaming terminology including:

  • FOV
  • FPS Limit
  • VSync
  • VFX Quality
  • Resolution
  • Fullscreen
  • Large Text

The goal is not to hide useful information.

The goal is to show players the information they actually need.

SDL3 FOUNDATION

Sector Rot continues moving toward its SDL3-based foundation.

Work has been completed across:

  • Rendering
  • Fonts
  • Images
  • Audio
  • Input
  • Display handling
  • Resolution support
  • Window management
  • Visual effects

Several native shutdown and resource-cleanup issues were also repaired.

A Windows crash caused by resources being destroyed in an unsafe order during shutdown was investigated and the cleanup sequence was rebuilt.

STABILITY & CRASH FIXES

A large number of stability issues have been addressed since Alpha 0.8.0.

This includes fixes for:

  • Native shutdown crashes
  • Audio cleanup
  • Duplicate resource destruction
  • Death-state problems
  • PDA resizing
  • World Conditions input
  • Reputation persistence
  • Open Run economy persistence
  • Multiplayer environment synchronization
  • Save migration
  • Sector cache migration
  • Player progression persistence
  • Large Text layouts

SAVE & WORLD PERSISTENCE

Open Run progression has been expanded while preserving existing player progression wherever possible.

Persistent systems include things such as:

  • Reputation
  • Scrap Credits
  • Contracts
  • Charters
  • Deeds
  • Territory
  • Domain progression

World-generation improvements can rebuild old cached sector layouts when required without intentionally deleting the player's long-term progression.

CREATOR TOOLS

Work has also continued on the tools used to build Sector Rot.

Improvements have been made to:

  • Sector Rot Game Editor
  • Internal Editor
  • Public Map Maker
  • Mod Tools
  • Content editing
  • Faction editing
  • NPC editing
  • Workspace tools

Player distributions are also being kept separate from developer and modding documentation so normal players receive only the documentation relevant to playing the game.

PACKAGING & RELEASE STABILITY

The release pipeline has received significant cleanup.

Player progress and save files can no longer accidentally be included inside the base game data package.

Builds now keep player data separate from packaged game content.

The installer, portable builds and content packaging have also received additional validation.

FROM ALPHA 0.8.0 TO ALPHA 0.9.0

Alpha 0.8.0 was an important foundation.

Alpha 0.9.0 is where many of those foundations finally begin working together.

Open Run now has:

A world to explore.

Factions to work with.

Territory to own.

A reason to become powerful.

A real long-term objective.

And finally, an ending.

There is still a lot more we want to build.

But Alpha 0.9.0 represents a major step toward the Sector Rot experience we want the game to become.

Thank you to everyone playing, testing, reporting problems and following development.

See you in the sectors.

updates.title: Sector Rot Version Alpha 0.8.0 – Major Update
updates.text:
Sector Rot Version Alpha 0.8.0 – Major Update

Hello, survivors!

Sector Rot Version Alpha 0.8.0 is now available.

This is the first complete development update since Alpha 0.7.8, and it represents a major expansion of the game rather than a small maintenance patch.

Alpha 0.8.0 introduces real LAN and Direct-IP multiplayer, a persistent Open Run Living Zone, original factions, territories, contracts, traders, dynamic conflicts, improved AI, tactical real-time survival, expanded procedural world generation, a redesigned inventory, stronger accessibility support, improved weapon VFX and many stability fixes.

The public version remains:

Sector Rot Version Alpha 0.8.0

Original Factions and Living Zone

Open Run now contains a persistent Living Zone populated by original factions, unaffiliated survivors, traders, guards, patrols, mutants and hostile raiders.

Players can begin an Open Run aligned with one of the following routes:

Independent

An unaffiliated survivor route for players who do not want to begin under the protection of an organised faction.

Independent players do not automatically receive faction territory, faction traders, protected compounds or faction contracts.

Veil Wardens

A disciplined faction focused on containment, observation and protection against the spreading Rot.

Rustbound Union

A practical industrial faction built around scavenging, repair, trade and survival through machinery and resources.

Null Chorus

A secretive faction connected to signals, anomalies and the stranger aspects of the affected sectors.

Black Road

Black Road is a hostile, non-playable raider faction.

Their bandits may attack faction territory, raid districts and appear during dynamic Living Zone events.

Faction identity is now used consistently throughout:

  • Open Run setup
  • Player information
  • Persistent saves
  • PDA records
  • Territory ownership
  • NPC dialogue
  • Contracts
  • Reputation
  • Trading
  • Dynamic events
  • Multiplayer world state

Persistent PDA System

Open Run now includes a persistent PDA interface.

The PDA provides access to:

  • Active and available contracts
  • Completed and archived missions
  • Faction reputation
  • Relationships between factions
  • Known contacts
  • Discovered territories
  • Active world events
  • Faction conflicts
  • Battle reports
  • Scrap Credits
  • Local economic information

Contract progress is connected to real gameplay actions such as:

  • Killing hostile enemies
  • Fighting mutants
  • Searching containers
  • Discovering districts
  • Defending territory
  • Clearing nests
  • Participating in Living Zone events

The PDA is available through a configurable key binding, with P used by default.

Faction Compounds, NPCs and Traders

Organised factions can control large, readable compounds containing:

  • Fenced territory
  • Guarded entrances
  • Exterior guard posts
  • Patrol routes
  • Multiple buildings
  • Protected rooms
  • Mission contacts
  • Quartermasters
  • Shelter areas

Quartermasters are located inside protected areas and use a dedicated face-to-face trading interface.

Trade is no longer performed through the PDA.

The new trading system includes:

  • Separate BUY and SELL sections
  • Local stock
  • Local demand
  • Item quantities
  • Owned quantities
  • Purchase prices
  • Selling rewards
  • Affordability information
  • Faction and territory market conditions

The Living Zone economy uses Scrap Credits.

NPC contacts and mission-givers provide full dialogue and faction work, while ordinary guards use shorter field responses.

Territory Control and Faction Wars

Organised factions now control deterministic macro-regions across the Open Run world.

Normal sectors contain no more than one organised faction presence.

Frontier sectors may contain two rival faction regions positioned on opposite sides of the map, separated by a large no-man’s-land.

Dynamic conflicts can include:

  • Faction assaults
  • Territory defence
  • Black Road raids
  • Mutant hordes
  • Nest-clearing operations
  • Protect-the-area contracts
  • Attacker and defender rally orders
  • Persistent battle reports

Faction-war actors move toward the contested area instead of remaining static.

The PDA reports:

  • Attacking faction
  • Defending faction
  • Contested territory
  • Force sizes
  • Current battle state
  • Resolved battle results
  • Regional control

The player’s starting safehouse appears only in the initial sector and is no longer copied repeatedly throughout the world.

Improved NPC and Mutant Simulation

Human NPCs and mutants now participate in a more active world simulation.

Human NPC improvements include:

  • Deterministic pathfinding
  • Exterior patrol routes
  • Guard-post behaviour
  • Gate-watching routines
  • Building entry
  • Interior movement
  • Building exit routes
  • Door interaction
  • Stuck detection
  • New destination selection
  • Emission shelter behaviour
  • Rally orders during wars and raids

Mutant improvements include:

  • Independent roaming
  • Player and NPC target selection
  • Pack-alert behaviour
  • Threat sharing between nearby creatures
  • Species-specific movement capabilities
  • Door interaction rules
  • Toxic-terrain rules
  • Migration behaviour
  • Reduced update frequency for distant ecology

Faction patrols can fight mutants.

Mutants can attack faction NPCs.

Hostile factions can fight one another.

The world is no longer simulated only around the player.

Dynamic Emission Storms

Emission Storms now have persistent visual and gameplay presentation.

During an active Emission:

  • The environment changes visually
  • Warning effects remain active between actions
  • Unsheltered characters can take damage
  • NPCs search for valid shelter
  • Visibility can be reduced
  • Buildings can provide protection

Only valid building interiors count as shelter.

Roads, open yards, gates and exterior fenced areas do not protect the player.

Accessibility settings can reduce the flash intensity, decorative motion and screen shake produced by these events.

Expanded Open Run World Generation

Open Run generation has been substantially redesigned.

Worlds remain seed-based, persistent and survival-focused, with selectable virtual sizes ranging from:

  • 100K Zone
  • Larger intermediate world presets
  • Up to 5M cells per axis

The game now uses:

  • Eight deterministic biome profiles
  • Six sector archetypes
  • Organised faction regions
  • Frontier sectors
  • Neutral wilderness
  • Mutant nests
  • Hazard districts
  • Ruined areas
  • Toxic zones
  • Anomaly zones
  • Roads and infrastructure
  • Persistent sector coordinates

Different sectors now vary through independent rules for:

  • Building density
  • Intact buildings
  • Ruined buildings
  • Open districts
  • Hazard locations
  • Toxic pools
  • Roads
  • Points of interest
  • Faction presence
  • Hostile ecology

Normal sectors no longer reuse the same repeated layout.

Cleaner and More Readable Sectors

Procedural generation has been adjusted to remove artificial map clutter.

Changes include:

  • Crates and barrels are no longer used as random floor decoration
  • Ambient terrain remains walkable
  • Containers are placed deliberately
  • POI density is limited
  • Compound density is limited
  • Room decoration is controlled
  • Toxic pools form readable clusters
  • Anomaly zones use clearer layouts
  • Neutral ruins no longer copy entire faction compounds
  • Intact buildings keep coherent walls and doorways
  • Roads cannot overwrite intact building walls
  • Mobile NPCs spawn on navigable cells
  • Patrols prefer locations with multiple exits

Terminals are now purposeful pieces of infrastructure.

A sector contains no more than two terminals, and most sectors contain none.

Terminals and power nodes are solid objects that must be used from an adjacent tile.

Reciprocal Sector Routes

Adjacent Open Run sectors now share reciprocal world-edge routes.

Leaving one sector and returning through the same world edge produces a matching connection instead of an unrelated transition.

Possible route types include:

  • Broken roads
  • Dirt trails
  • Rail tunnels
  • Bunker passages
  • Drainage culverts
  • Abandoned checkpoints
  • Cave cuts
  • Service gates

Route type and placement are determined by the world seed and shared edge identity.

Routes remain navigable, but they are not guaranteed safe corridors.

Enemies and hazards may still appear near a transition.

Turn-Based and Real-Time Survival

Single-player Open Run now supports two simulation modes:

Turn-Based

The traditional tactical Sector Rot experience.

The world advances through player actions.

Real-Time Survival

Enemies, mutants, factions, emissions, events and world time continue to advance through a fixed simulation clock.

Player movement remains tactical and grid-based:

  • A quick key press performs one step
  • Holding a direction begins controlled movement after a short delay
  • Continued movement performs one tactical action at a time
  • Movement is not tied to rendering FPS
  • Windows keyboard repeat does not control player speed
  • Releasing the key immediately stops movement
  • Diagonal movement preserves corner-blocking rules

Single-player Pause and Settings screens freeze the real-time simulation.

Multiplayer cannot pause the authoritative world.

Campaign remains fully turn-based.

Death, Lives and Respawning

Open Run now supports multiple life rules:

  • One Life
  • 3 Lives
  • 5 Lives
  • Infinite Lives

One Life is the hardcore option.

When that survivor dies, they are permanently removed from the current world.

Finite lives are tracked independently for every multiplayer player.

When lives remain, players can choose:

  • Respawn Here
  • Respawn at Start

Respawning applies a full survival penalty:

  • Collected weapons are removed
  • Ammunition is removed
  • Armor is removed
  • Keycards are removed
  • Carried loot is removed
  • Health is restored
  • The minimum melee fallback is provided

Death and respawn stability has also been improved:

  • Death is processed only once
  • Duplicate death callbacks have been removed
  • Health cannot continue falling below zero
  • Pending movement is cleared
  • Held movement is cancelled
  • Real-time simulation stops during the death transition
  • Real-time simulation restarts after respawn
  • Returning to the Main Menu clears remaining gameplay timers

Real LAN and Direct-IP Multiplayer

Alpha 0.8.0 introduces real TCP networking.

Players can host and join through:

  • Local Area Network
  • Direct IPv4 connection
  • Hamachi
  • Radmin VPN
  • Other compatible virtual LAN tools

The multiplayer foundation now includes:

  • Real SectorRot_Server.exe TCP server
  • Join by IP
  • Optional server password
  • Server invitation information
  • Exact version validation
  • Network protocol validation
  • Enabled-mod hash validation
  • Persistent player identity
  • Persistent world snapshots
  • Host reconnection
  • Server recovery snapshots
  • Automatic authority migration while the server companion remains active
  • Saved multiplayer worlds
  • REHOST support
  • Multiplayer latency information
  • Scrollable Saved Worlds interface

The server owns the authoritative simulation.

Clients submit actions rather than independently simulating world events.

Synchronised systems include:

  • Players
  • Enemies
  • Faction NPCs
  • Mutants
  • Doors
  • Terminals
  • Items
  • Containers
  • Shared map state
  • Territories
  • Contracts
  • World events
  • Player lives

Supported network actions include:

  • Movement
  • Melee
  • Directional shooting
  • Weapon selection
  • Pickup
  • Interaction
  • Waiting
  • Medkit use

Open Co-op uses the host’s Open Run world size, life rule and simulation mode.

The interface permits up to 64 players, but the recommended Alpha range remains 8–32 players until additional real multi-PC stress testing is completed.

Inventory, Containers and Equipment

The inventory has been rebuilt into a clearer multi-column interface.

Items are separated into categories such as:

  • Weapons
  • Ammunition
  • Supplies
  • Mission items

The inventory now includes:

  • Selected-item details
  • Weapon statistics
  • Ammunition information
  • Current equipment
  • Contextual actions
  • Equip Weapon
  • Use Medkit
  • Clearer health and armor information

Container interaction now includes:

  • Selected-item inspection
  • TAKE SELECTED
  • TAKE ALL
  • Clear item quantities
  • Better action feedback

A Living Zone inventory crash caused by the reworked inventory connection has also been fixed.

Weapon VFX Improvements

Weapon effects are now connected directly to real gameplay firing.

VFX can appear when:

  • A shot hits an enemy
  • A shot hits a wall
  • A shot hits another obstacle
  • A shot misses

Weapons now have more distinct visual identities:

Pistol

  • Compact muzzle flash
  • Precise tracer
  • Controlled impact
  • Single casing feedback

Shotgun

  • Wide muzzle blast
  • Visible pellet spread
  • Strong impact burst
  • Heavier recoil and smoke

SMG

  • Multi-shot burst presentation
  • Repeated tracer impulses
  • Multiple casing effects
  • Rapid impact feedback

Rifle

  • Long tracer
  • Strong after-image
  • Sharper impact
  • More focused muzzle effect

Knife

  • Directional slash
  • Close-range impact burst
  • Distinct melee presentation

VFX Quality can be configured as Low, Medium or High.

Quality changes presentation density without changing damage, accuracy or gameplay simulation.

Larger Field of View

The tactical FOV system has been expanded.

Changes include:

  • Increased default visibility
  • Slightly improved class visibility
  • FOV settings available up to 18
  • Environment and weather visibility modifiers
  • FOV-related perks and bonuses

This allows players to display more of the tactical environment while preserving grid-based movement and combat.

Classes, Perks and Achievements

The character catalogue has been expanded to:

  • 10 playable classes
  • 10 functional perks
  • 12 mutant and monster families
  • 17 achievement icons and tracked achievements

Newer perks include:

  • Scrap Plating
  • Stormwise
  • Broker’s Eye
  • Second Wind

Perks can affect:

  • Maximum health
  • Armor capacity
  • Starting equipment
  • Container interaction speed
  • Pickup speed
  • FOV
  • Medkit healing
  • Enemy detection
  • Emission resistance
  • Trading prices

Player Stats has also been redesigned with:

  • Clearer totals
  • Achievement progress
  • Perk cards
  • Progress bars
  • Native achievement artwork
  • Locked and unlocked states

UI and Accessibility Overhaul

Settings have been reorganised into five categories:

  • Display
  • Performance
  • Audio
  • Controls
  • Accessibility

Accessibility options include:

  • Large Text
  • Reduced Motion
  • Flash Intensity
  • Screen Shake
  • High Contrast
  • Color-vision presets
  • Auto Pickup
  • Confirm Exit
  • Rebindable controls

Large Text has been reviewed across:

  • Main Menu
  • Settings
  • Accessibility
  • Gameplay
  • Inventory
  • Containers
  • NPC dialogue
  • Trading
  • PDA
  • Open Run setup

Layouts were adjusted to prevent:

  • Text clipping
  • Broken button rows
  • Overlapping elements
  • Content leaving its container
  • Missing final lines

Internal Guard and Mutant population counters have also been removed from the player-facing information box.

Main Menu and Visual Presentation

The Main Menu now includes:

  • Animated Sector Rot wordmark deformation
  • Large rotating pseudo-3D ASCII Earth
  • Conflict hot zones
  • Reduced Motion support
  • Visible Discord and itch.io controls
  • Updated Alpha 0.8.0 presentation

SDL3 text rendering has also been improved through:

  • Integer font sizes
  • Solid glyph rasterisation
  • Monospaced font hinting
  • Pixel-aligned rendering
  • Natural-width ASCII glyphs
  • Reduced stretching and blur

Performance Foundation

The ASCII renderer no longer creates and updates thousands of individual text objects for every map frame.

The new SDL3 rendering foundation uses:

  • Persistent glyph atlas
  • Retained viewport texture
  • Dirty-cell updates
  • Camera texture shifting
  • Cached map metrics
  • Reduced geometry rebuilding
  • Reduced duplicate redraws
  • Throttled autosaves
  • Bounded AI pathfinding
  • Bounded actor updates
  • Lower-frequency distant ecology
  • Compact multiplayer state deltas

The same retained map path is used by:

  • The game
  • Internal Editor
  • Public Map Maker

Performance settings now include additional frame-rate targets and a native 1920×1080 performance audit.

Internal Editor, Public Map Maker and Modding

The creator tools have also been expanded.

Internal Editor and Public Map Maker now support:

  • Map resizing up to 2048×2048
  • Independent viewport zoom
  • Larger map workflows
  • Improved validation
  • Data packing
  • Public documentation rebuilding
  • Mod validation
  • Map validation
  • Standalone Player builds
  • Windows Installer builds
  • Standalone release ZIP creation

The project also includes expanded documentation for:

  • Map creation
  • Tile data
  • Symbols
  • Weapons
  • Enemies
  • Classes
  • Perks
  • Campaign
  • Open Run
  • Multiplayer
  • Mod packaging
  • Testing
  • Branding
  • Build and installer workflows

Recent Stability Fixes

The current Alpha 0.8.0 package also includes fixes for several recently reported problems:

  • Loading a recent Open Run now restarts the world simulation
  • The player no longer moves while enemies and NPCs remain frozen
  • Bandits using the 5 symbol are identified correctly
  • Bandits remain hostile and attackable
  • Bandits no longer display dialogue belonging to a different faction
  • Inventory selection no longer calls a missing function
  • Death no longer causes repeated callbacks
  • Respawn restores the correct simulation state
  • Held movement no longer becomes uncontrolled real-time running
  • Weapon VFX now activate through real firing paths
  • Large Text layouts no longer break the tested UI containers
  • Player-facing information no longer displays internal population counters

Current Alpha Multiplayer Limitations

Alpha 0.8.0 does not yet include:

  • Public matchmaking
  • NAT traversal
  • Official relay servers
  • Automatic mod downloading
  • Encrypted network traffic

Direct internet hosting may require TCP port forwarding and may not work through CGNAT.

Do not reuse sensitive passwords as multiplayer server passwords.

A stopped persistent server world must be started again through REHOST.

Thank you to everyone testing Sector Rot and reporting problems.

Alpha 0.8.0 is a major foundation update for the future of Open Run, Living Zone, multiplayer, factions and the wider Sector Rot world.

More content, balancing, world events, multiplayer testing and improvements will continue in future updates.

— FATHER

games.title: The Outsiders
games.short: You are a member of iNSIDERS CORPORATION, an organization that collects and investigates strange anomaly objects and locations.
description: You are a member of iNSIDERS CORPORATION, an organization that collects and investigates strange anomaly objects and locations.
Your partner went missing after he was sent to investigate an anomalous city to gather the Object, but it didn't went good for him and you were selected for his rescue.

Everything is dull, dead, suspended in a silence that presses down on you. No life. No movement. But something is hidden there, and you need to uncover it and maybe, if there's still time, find your partner. If they're still alive...

updates.title: The Outsiders - Pre-Alpha 0.6.2
updates.text:
Hello everybody!

Recently i've been working on implement the foundation for introduction to Chapters!

Right now the main loop is ready to go and the only things that is not in Version 0.6.2 is the Map and the Story for Chapter 2.

Things reworked / updated / introduced in Version 0.6.2:

  • New Chapter Select Monitor / Screen (In wich you can select what chapters you can play, only Chapter 1 is visible).
  • Reworked some aspects of the Player HUD - Added an BodyCam recording icon + little informations.
  • Implemented the AmbientSounds in the Forest area (If the sounds are not working / not hearing them let me know).
  • Reworked the Main Menu icons and added the IndieDB logo + link to the project.

In the next update, Version 0.6.3 i will add an Head Bobbing Slider (To stop or lower the Head Bobbing sway)

The Chapter 1, might get a rework after the foundations is set for the Chapter 2 (Might improve some aspects on in-game items and or story).



Thank you!

updates.text:
